chunks: He said: And Bahr ibn Ziyad al-Tahhan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Marwan from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A man said: May I be your ransom, people narrate that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said in Kufa on the pulpit: 'If only one day remained from the world, Allah would prolong that day until Allah sends a man from me who will fill it with justice and equity, just as it was filled with oppression and injustice.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Yes. He asked: Are you that one? He said: No, he is the namesake of the Splitter of the Sea.

key_terms.الْفَالِقِ الْبَحْر: The Splitter of the Sea (a title for the Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: Who is the 'man from me' that will fill the earth with justice according to Imam Ali's sermon in Kufa?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir, the famous prophetic tradition regarding the Mahdi's global reign of justice is confirmed, with a crucial distinction made between the current Imam and the future savior. By identifying the Mahdi as 'Sami al-Falq al-Bahr' (the Splitter of the Sea), Tusi highlights the specific eschatological identity of Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, distinguishing him from his father to refute the Waqifiya who claimed the Imamate ended with al-Baqir. This clarification underscores the continuity of the Imamate and the unique role of the Twelfth Imam in Shia eschatology.
